description: Character-confusion matrix and cost model for SAAKSHI's weighted plate edit distance (D2-04). Config, not code: this file is read from disk at runtime, so changing a cost changes ranking with no rebuild. Every pair carries its own provenance — nothing here is a guess about Indian plates in general, it is what this estate was measured to do plus what is directly derivable from the D2-03 correction maps.

sources.measured: D2-01 (#15) / D2-05 (#19) — confusions observed on the sandbox estate's own output. n is small (3 human-legible plates over 120 hand-labelled vehicle instances); docs/anpr-accuracy.md carries the denominators.
sources.derived-cross-class: packages/shared/src/plate/grammar.ts ALPHA_TO_DIGIT / DIGIT_TO_ALPHA (D2-03, #17), including each entry's `alternatives`. A glyph pair the corrector is willing to repair is a glyph pair the search must be willing to cross.
sources.derived-alpha-bridge: Two letters are confusable with each other when ALPHA_TO_DIGIT maps them (or their alternatives) to the same digit — they are the same shape by transitivity. This is how the alpha-to-alpha confusions get modelled at all: they never change a character's class, so D2-03's slot-aware corrector is structurally blind to them.
sources.closure: C and E are both measured as read `F`, so they are confusable with each other.

notModelled.digitToDigit: No digit-to-digit pair is modelled. None was measured on this estate and none is derivable from the correction maps (no two digits share a letter in DIGIT_TO_ALPHA). 1/7 and 5/6 are plausible on other estates; they are absent here because inventing them would be an accuracy claim without a measurement. This is a known gap, stated in docs/fuzzy-matching.md.
